name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Bronin's overwhelming fundraising edge ($3.7M raised vs about $21K for Chai)
Open seat after Larson's primary loss adds transition uncertainty
Markets price roughly 95% Democratic; no public general-election polls
model.rationale: The district's twelve-point Democratic lean, Bronin's massive financial advantage, and market pricing near 95 percent all point to a comfortable hold despite the open seat; with no polls available, uncertainty stays elevated but not enough to threaten the outcome.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Bronin or signs that the open-seat transition is costing Democrats enthusiasm could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's first district is an open seat after John Larson lost renomination, but it remains firmly Democratic terrain with a partisan lean of twelve points. Luke Bronin, a former Hartford mayor, enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $3.7 million and drawn substantial outside support, while Republican Amy Chai has raised roughly $21,000 and reported only a few hundred dollars on hand. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price the Democratic nominee around 95 percent. Outside spending against Bronin has been modest, and nothing in the record suggests a genuinely contested race. The forecast expects a comfortable Democratic hold, with the open-seat transition the main source of uncertainty.
